items.title: Google AI leaks "scarily accurate and very specific" game detail from private documents, says indie dev
items.excerpt: An indie dev says Google's AI surfaced an unannounced project name that existed only in their private documents. A hard question for any studio piping design docs through cloud AI tooling.

items.title: Nexus Mods finally tightens the screws on AI, though it's still playing softball with the tide of slop
items.excerpt: Nexus Mods split its generative-AI tag into finer labels and warned that failure to disclose AI usage may trigger moderation. Metadata design as the front line of UGC AI policy.

items.title: The voice of Shinji in Evangelion says AI voice cloning is 'heartbreaking,' calls for Japanese government to intervene
items.excerpt: Megumi Ogata calls AI voice cloning 'heartbreaking' and asks Japan's government to regulate it, as synthetic voice pipelines spread through games and anime production.

items.title: NVIDIA releases its RTX Neural Texture Compression SDK for the ARM64 platform
items.excerpt: NVIDIA shipped its RTX Neural Texture Compression SDK for ARM64 ahead of RTX Spark laptops, letting developers keep high-res texture detail at a fraction of the VRAM. Neural asset compression moves into shipping art pipelines.

items.title: Into the Omniverse: How Open World Models Push the Frontier of Physical AI
items.excerpt: NVIDIA lays out how downloadable, inspectable open world models are becoming the substrate for simulated 3D environments in Omniverse. The same world-model stack now underwriting generative game worlds.

items.title: Game AI Expert on Where AI Actually Belongs in Game Development
items.excerpt: Luke Dicken, who has researched game AI for decades, maps where generative AI genuinely fits in production pipelines and player personalization — and argues the industry's biggest opportunity is not replacing human talent.

items.title: Design Arena creators raise $7.9 million to bring taste to AI models
items.excerpt: Founders who tried to build an AI game engine found the models could make functional games that were never fun — so they built Design Arena, now 5.3M users strong, to feed human taste judgments back to frontier labs.

items.title: Ethical Usage of Image and Video Models to Accelerate Workflows | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
items.excerpt: An Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 session on folding Tripo 3.1, Nano Banana and ChatGPT Images 2.0 into an art production pipeline without wrecking authorship. A practical ethics-plus-workflow talk for game art teams.

items.title: From Words to Worlds: Integrating MCP into the Unreal Editor | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
items.excerpt: Unreal Engine 5.8 ships an official Model Context Protocol integration plus new PCG spatial primitives, letting models like Claude operate inside the editor on Blueprints, levels, materials and meshes while everything stays editable.

items.title: MetaHuman in 2026: Five Years In, What's Next? | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
items.excerpt: Epic traces MetaHuman's shift from experiment to production standard for digital humans across games, film and real-time work, and sketches where the ML-driven animation and creator tooling go next.

items.title: NVIDIA's AI Learns Why Copying Humans Isn't Enough
items.excerpt: A walkthrough of NVIDIA-backed research on human-interaction motion learning that goes beyond imitating mocap clips — the kind of learned motion work that feeds real-time character animation in games.

items.title: Opening Unity to everyone - one API, every role
items.excerpt: Unity is opening the Editor beyond the Editor: one API and a set of services so every role — and every agent or script — can drive the same project surface. Groundwork for AI-assisted pipelines around Unity 7.
